analysis.subject: biology
analysis.pageCoverage: Page explains that cells are basic building blocks with many specialized parts and describes functions of cytoplasm, cytoskeleton, endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi apparatus, lysosomes and peroxisomes, mitochondria, nucleus, plasma membrane and ribosomes.

overview.headline: Cells as building blocks and their specialized parts

keyPoints.point: Cells provide structure, take in nutrients, convert nutrients into energy and carry out specialized functions.
keyPoints.quote: They provide structure for the body, take in nutrients from food, convert those nutrients into energy, and carry out specialized functions.

keyPoints.point: The nucleus acts as the command center that sends directions for growth and division and houses hereditary material.
keyPoints.quote: The nucleus serves as the cell’s command center, sending directions to the cell to grow, mature, divide, or die.

keyPoints.point: Mitochondria convert energy from food into a usable form and contain their own genetic material.
keyPoints.quote: Mitochondria are complex organelles that convert energy from food into a form that the cell can use.

keyPoints.point: The cytoskeleton forms the structural framework that determines cell shape and allows movement and division.
keyPoints.quote: The cytoskeleton is a network of long fibers that make up the cell’s structural framework.

keyTerms.gloss: jelly-like fluid and structures that surround the nucleus
keyTerms.quote: Within cells, the cytoplasm is made up of a jelly-like fluid (called the cytosol) and other structures that surround the nucleus.

keyTerms.gloss: network of fibers forming the structural framework of the cell
keyTerms.quote: The cytoskeleton is a network of long fibers that make up the cell’s structural framework.

keyTerms.gloss: organelles that convert energy from food into usable form
keyTerms.quote: Mitochondria are complex organelles that convert energy from food into a form that the cell can use.

keyTerms.gloss: command center that houses hereditary material and directs growth and division
keyTerms.quote: The nucleus serves as the cell’s command center, sending directions to the cell to grow, mature, divide, or die.

keyTerms.gloss: organelles that process genetic instructions to create proteins
keyTerms.quote: Ribosomes are organelles that process the cell’s genetic instructions to create proteins.

keyTerms.gloss: outer lining that separates the cell from its environment
keyTerms.quote: The plasma membrane is the outer lining of the cell.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Reinforces core facts about cell functions and parts so students can recall definitions and roles.
componentPlan.focusQuote: Cells are the basic building blocks of all living things.

componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: Helps students link processing and transport relationships between endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi and other organelles.
componentPlan.focusQuote: The Golgi apparatus packages molecules processed by the endoplasmic reticulum to be transported out of the cell.
